title: Safety and Efficacy Study of Gantenerumab in Participants With Early Alzheimer's Disease (AD)
one_line: A Phase 3 trial of gantenerumab in early Alzheimer's disease was terminated after showing significant reduction in amyloid plaques and CSF biomarkers but failing to demonstrate a statistically significant slowing of clinical decline on the CDR-SB.
summary: This Phase III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (NCT03443973) evaluated the safety and efficacy of subcutaneous gantenerumab in 975 patients with early Alzheimer's disease. Over 116 weeks, participants received either gantenerumab with gradual up-titration or a matching placebo. Gantenerumab successfully reduced amyloid burden as measured by PET (-56.46 centiloids difference from placebo) and positively altered CSF biomarkers including pTau-181, tTau, neurogranin, and NFL. Despite these robust biomarker changes, the drug did not meet its primary clinical efficacy endpoint. The adjusted mean difference on the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) at week 116 was -0.19, which failed to reach statistical significance (p=0.2998). While some secondary clinical endpoints like ADAS-Cog13 and FAQ showed nominal numerical advantages, overall clinical benefit was insufficient. Gantenerumab treatment also resulted in higher rates of ARIA-E and ARIA-H compared to placebo. Consequently, Hoffmann-La Roche terminated the trial and development of gantenerumab for early Alzheimer's disease.

key_claims.claim: Gantenerumab failed to significantly slow clinical decline on the primary cognitive endpoint.
key_claims.evidence: Adjusted mean difference on CDR-SB at Week 116 was -0.19 (95% CI -0.55 to 0.17), p=0.2998.
key_claims.location: PRIMARY: DBT Period: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Global Outcome, as Measured by CDR-SB

key_claims.claim: Gantenerumab significantly reduced brain amyloid load.
key_claims.evidence: Difference in adjusted means for amyloid PET was -56.46 centiloids (95% CI -64.36 to -48.56), p<0.0001.
key_claims.location: SECONDARY: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Brain Amyloid Load as Measured by Amyloid Positron Emission Tomography (PET) Scan

key_claims.claim: Gantenerumab improved multiple downstream CSF biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease.
key_claims.evidence: Percent difference in geometric means compared to placebo: NFL -13.2% (p=0.014), Neurogranin -14.4% (p<0.001), tTau -17.8% (p<0.001), pTau-181 -21.0% (p<0.001).
key_claims.location: SECONDARY: DBT Period: Percent Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) Marker of Disease

key_claims.claim: Gantenerumab did not significantly alter regional brain tau load as measured by PET.
key_claims.evidence: Differences in adjusted means for tau PET across temporal, medial temporal, frontal, and parietal regions ranged from 0.00 to 0.01 (all p>0.05).
key_claims.location: SECONDARY: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Brain Tau Load, as Measured by Tau PET Scan

key_claims.claim: Gantenerumab treatment increased the incidence of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).
key_claims.evidence: ARIA-E occurred in 128 gantenerumab vs 18 placebo participants; ARIA-H occurred in 109 gantenerumab vs 57 placebo participants.
key_claims.location: SECONDARY: DBT Period: Number of Participants With ARIA-E / ARIA-H Confirmed by MRI

methods.design: Phase III, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group
methods.population: Patients aged 50-90 with prodromal to mild Alzheimer's disease, MMSE ≥ 22, CDR-GS 0.5 or 1.0, and evidence of beta-amyloid pathology.

funding_and_conflicts: Hoffmann-La Roche (Lead sponsor). No specific author conflicts of interest are stated in this registry record.
limitations: The trial was terminated early following a pre-planned analysis of safety and efficacy in the Graduate I & II programs.
Tau PET analysis was conducted at a pooled level with another study (WN29922), meaning the specific results shown represent the combined population rather than just this trial.

issues: Document is a well-formatted API extraction of a ClinicalTrials.gov record, lacking the usual PDF-to-Markdown artifacts.
